questions.r2: Is there a console.log whose argument is the bracketed expression (2 + 2) * 3, with the brackets around the 2 + 2? console.log(2 + 2 * 3) without brackets alone is NO. What any comment says, or whether there is a comment at all, does not matter. Other console.log lines are fine.

questions.r6: Is the variable stuff gone from the code: never declared, assigned or used? The word stuff may still appear in a comment as ordinary prose, and that is fine. Names like maxScore, playerName or levelCount are irrelevant.

questions.r2: Ignore any console.log that is only a heading or label (like "My answers:"). Among the remaining logs, which are the paradigm answers, is the SECOND one the text object-oriented (any capital letters, or object oriented with a space)? Code in comments never runs.

questions.r1: Ignore any console.log that is only a heading or label (like "My answers:"). Among the remaining logs, is the FIRST one the text procedural (any capital letters)? Code in comments never runs.

questions.r4: Is there a REAL for loop (for (...) { ... } written as code, not as text) whose body contains a console.log, possibly inside an if? A log only after the loop ends means no. Program text written inside a console.log("...") string is only printed words, not a loop: NO.
questions.r5: Is there a REAL while loop (written as code, not as text) whose body adds another value to a variable on each pass, like total = total + n or total += n, where that variable is not just the loop counter stepping by one? Adding after the loop ends means no. Program text written inside a console.log("...") string is only words: NO.

questions.r8: For a filament the switch recognises, does the program print (console.log) a recommended temperature with an actual number, such as "Temperature: 200"? The number may be printed inside the case or after the switch from a variable the case set. Printing only the word "temperature" with no value, or printing from code that can never run, means no. A case may instead return the text for a console.log of the call to print: that is YES, and a switch(true) with comparisons counts. A console.log standing outside any switch, because the whole switch is commented out, is NO.
questions.r9: For a filament the switch recognises, does the program print (console.log) a recommended print speed with an actual number, such as "Speed: 60"? The number may be printed inside the case or after the switch from a variable the case set. Printing only the word "speed" with no value, or printing from code that can never run, means no. A case may instead return the text for a console.log of the call to print: that is YES, and a switch(true) with comparisons counts. A console.log standing outside any switch, because the whole switch is commented out, is NO.
questions.r10: Is there a comment that says what WOULD run or print if a case's break were removed? It must name the effect: the next case's, or the default's, output would run or print too ('it falls into ABS, so both print', 'it would also print Unknown'). NO if it only names the idea without the effect ('break removed falls through', 'fall through without stop', a list of switch keywords), or says nothing would print, or the switch would stop or error. NO if the switch is commented out.

questions.r2: Is an arrow function with a one-expression body (no { } braces) itself handed to transform as its argument: written inside the call, or a const's NAME passed with no parentheses after it? If the argument is plus(1), a call that already ran the arrow, no function was passed: NO. If the arrow's body is in braces: NO.

Look at every arrow function (=>) in the code. Is every arrow's body a bare expression, not a { } block? A body in round brackets like n => ({ v: n }) is still a bare expression. The body may start on the next line. Function declarations with the function keyword are not arrows, ignore them. NO if any arrow has a { } block body.

questions.r4: Does a console.log print a field read off one item of order.items (order.items[i].name, or item.name where item is the loop variable)? A helper also counts: console.log(line(item)) where line(item) reads item.name and returns text. Both forms are YES. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.
questions.r5: Does a loop over order.items print a field read off each item (it.name, it.price, or a helper's text built from them)? console.log(it), which prints the whole item, is NO. A field read in a statement that is not printed (a line that is only order.items[0].name;) is NO. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r3: Look at the argument written inside describeBox( ... ) at its call: are curly braces typed right there, like describeBox({ width: 2, height: 3, color: 'red' })? A name such as describeBox(o) or describeBox(box) is NO, even though the name holds an object. The call must actually RUN (top level, or inside a function that a line calls; go() never called is NO), and its returned text must be printed: console.log(describeBox({...})) or stored then logged. A call whose result is never printed is NO; a describeBox that prints inside itself is NO.
questions.r4: Is there a console.log(...) call written as code anywhere in the file (not only inside a comment or inside quotes)? Whatever it prints is fine.

questions.r3: After the unpack, is each of the three names used on its own (no dot) in a printed sentence: a console.log of text built from them, or a variable built from them that is then printed? Printing typeof of the names does not count. A console.log inside a function counts only if that function is really called; naming it (typeof say) is not a call. Code inside comments never runs. A helper of your own that prints, called with the sentence, counts. If one of the three unpacked names is never used in anything printed, NO: a function that unpacks its own parameter with the same name is a different variable.

questions.r2: record fields read with a dot: console.log prints a record's field read with a dot (players[i].name, a record variable then a dot, or a helper that returns text read off its record), or the fields are unpacked from one record with braces. Code inside a comment, or written inside quotes as text, never runs. A helper's returned text stored in a variable that is then printed counts. console.log(p) or console.log(JSON.stringify(...)) prints the whole record: NO. A field read in a statement that is not printed is NO.
questions.r5: Is the code free of separate arrays of plain values (like const names = [...], const scores = [...], however made: a list in brackets, split, Array.of, new Set)? The data must live only in one array of record objects (players). Arrays of objects are fine. NO if any array of plain strings or numbers is still declared. Comments never count.

questions.r7: Is there a loop whose header contains Object.keys(...) of one record, whose body PRINTS (console.log) each value fetched with the key in square brackets, like console.log(key + ': ' + cart[0][key])? A bare read cart[0][key]; with no console.log, or values typed into separate console.log lines, is NO. A for...in loop is NO. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r3: Is there a loop whose header contains the words Object.keys(laptop) (a for, for...of or while loop: for (const k of Object.keys(laptop)), or a loop over a keys array made by Object.keys), that prints each value fetched with the key in square brackets (laptop[key] or laptop[keys[i]])? A for...in loop (for (const k in laptop)) is NO, because Object.keys is not in it. Printing only the key names, with the values typed in by hand, is NO. A loop in a function nobody calls is NO. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r6: Is the function structuredClone called anywhere in the code, including inside a function the student wrote (const copyBook = (b) => structuredClone(b), or function dupe(x) { return structuredClone(x); }), whatever those functions are named? YES for those. NO only if structuredClone never appears, or only inside a comment or quotes.

questions.r3: Is the left or right key ('a', 'd', 'left', 'right') read with kb.pressing (or similar) in code that really runs every frame: draw(), update(), or a function they call? Setup runs once: NO. Code written inside a console.log string or backtick template is only text and never runs: NO. Comments never run.
questions.r4: Is the up or down key ('w', 's', 'up', 'down') read with kb.pressing (or similar) in code that really runs every frame: draw(), update(), or a function they call? Setup runs once: NO. Code written inside a console.log string or backtick template is only text and never runs: NO. Comments never run.

questions.r6: Does the sprite that is NOT driven by the keys (the mover, any name) move on its own with no key held? YES if it is given a velocity or rotationSpeed, even once in setup() (a number, or a variable like mover.vel.x = speed), or its position changes every frame from frameCount or a nudge like mover.x += 1. NO if the motion is only inside an if that tests a key, or just copies the player's speed. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r3: Is background() called inside draw() (or in a function draw() or update() calls) with some colour? Any colour counts. Everything else in the program is irrelevant to this question. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.
questions.r1: Is a canvas created with new Canvas(...), in setup() or at the top of the file? Any size counts. NO if new Canvas appears only in a comment or in quotes.

questions.r3: Is there a new Sprite(x, y, w, h) whose SECOND number (the y) is positive, like new Sprite(-80, 120, 30, 30)? Only the second number matters. The x may be negative, and it does not matter whether the sprite is stored in a variable or whether later lines run correctly. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r1: Does setup() set world.gravity.y so things fall DOWN the screen? With the default origin, a positive number (like 10) is YES, zero or negative is NO. If the sketch sets world.origin = 'math' (y grows up) it flips: then only a NEGATIVE number is YES, and a positive number like 10 is NO because the ball rises. Comments never count.

questions.r3: Is each bumper's own worth added only on the frame a touch starts? Check how the bumper's memory (like b.hit) is updated. ball.colliding(b) returns a NUMBER, never false. If the memory is set straight from it (touching = ball.colliding(b); b.hit = touching) and the test is b.hit === false, it can never be false again after the first touch: NO. YES only if the memory is set to true/false itself (b.hit = touching > 0, or = true / false), or the test uses !, or the add is under ball.collides(b).

questions.r4: After a jump, does the code ask canJumpFrom (or an equivalent test) about the piece's NEW square, keeping the turn only when it says yes and passing the turn when it says no? If every jump keeps the turn (chain = true) without ever asking canJumpFrom, then NO. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r3: Read the test inside online.onMove((m, seat) => ...) that guards act. YES only if it compares the handler's own second parameter (the name in the parentheses, here seat) with turn AND checks the move: inline, or goodMove(m) whose body really tests that m.act is 1 to 3 and m.roll is 0 to 3. If it uses online.seat instead (this computer's own seat): NO. A goodMove that just returns true, or never looks at the roll: NO.
questions.r2: Inside online.onMove((m, seat) => ...), does the handler call act for the arriving move, directly or inside an if, so every move that arrives runs act on this computer? YES: online.onMove((m, seat) => { if (...) act(turn, m.act, m.roll); }). Extra conditions in the if are fine. NO: the handler only logs or stores m, or act is called only from the key handler and never from onMove.
questions.r4: Is there ONE test on duel that picks between two paths: in a duel the move is sent with online.send, otherwise act is called straight away? YES: if (duel) online.send({...}); else act(turn, a, roll);. NO: only online.send with no offline path, or act always called directly. Comments never run.

questions.r3: Does the code contain a console.log("Leap year") AND a separate console.log("Not a leap year"), each message printed by its own console.log (normally the two branches of an if / else)? Both messages must appear in console.log calls. Other lines do not matter.

questions.r2: Look for an if statement followed by at least two else if branches, like if (score >= 90) {...} else if (score >= 80) {...} else if (score >= 70) {...}. Does each else if branch test score against a number and print something with console.log? A final else is fine and does not count as a branch.
Does the program have a switch with at least one case label, like case 200: or case 'PLA':? Any number of cases and any values are fine. NO if the word case appears only in a comment.

questions.r3: Does pressing the R key call startRound()? There must be a test for the r key, like kb.presses('r') or key === 'r', that calls startRound(). startRound() merely being defined, or called once from setup(), is NOT enough: NO. Comments never run.

questions.r2: Inside online.onMove((m, seat) => ...), is doMove called for the arriving move (directly, or inside an if with other checks), so every move that arrives is applied on this computer? NO if doMove is only called from the click handler and never inside onMove, or if onMove only logs.
questions.r4: Is there ONE test on online.status that picks between two paths: when it is 'off' the move is made straight away with doMove, otherwise it is sent with online.send? YES: if (online.status === 'off') doMove(...); else online.send({...}). NO: only online.send, or only doMove. Comments never run.
Is there a console.log(...) call written as code anywhere in the file (not only inside a comment or inside quotes)? Whatever it prints is fine.

questions.r3: On the player's turn, is each of the keys 1, 2 and 3 tested (kb.presses('1'), kb.presses('2'), kb.presses('3'), or a loop or array over '1','2','3'), each leading to a different action (attack, guard, potion)? A helper called from draw or update counts. NO if only one or two keys are tested. Comments never run.
questions.r4: Does the enemy choose its action by a rule instead of always attacking: a potion when its hp is low, or a guard chosen by random()? YES if the enemy's turn has an if or random test that can lead to guard or potion. NO if the enemy always attacks. Comments never run.

questions.r5: Two things must both be there: (1) when a fighter's hp is 0 or less the battle is marked over (over = true, or an equivalent state); (2) once it is over, pressing R (kb.presses('r')) starts a new game (newGame or a reset). YES only if both are present. Comments never run.

questions.r3: Is after(frames, fn) called with a number of frames AND a function that runs later: a name like after(45, hitBack) or an arrow after(45, () => hitBack())? after(45, hitBack()) with the call parentheses is NO, because that passes the result, not the function. Any number and any function name are fine.

questions.r6: Does the writing state the exact final values the caller prints, the three numbers 0, 20, 30 (written 0, 20, 30 or [0, 20, 30])? All three numbers must appear as what the caller prints. NO if the numbers are missing or different, or if it only says 'back to the caller' without them.

questions.r3: Is there a variable (named rating, grade, or anything else) that is ASSIGNED a ternary chain, written as const x = score >= 90 ? ... : score >= 70 ? ... : ..., with the 90 cutoff tested before the 70 cutoff? NO if the chain is written straight inside console.log( ... ) with no variable holding it. NO if it is if / else if. NO if 70 is checked first. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.
questions.r4: Is a VARIABLE that holds the ternary chain's result passed to console.log (console.log(rating), or console.log(grade))? Any variable name counts. NO if the ternary is written straight inside console.log( ... ) so no variable holds it: console.log(score >= 90 ? 'A' : 'B') is NO. NO if only score is logged, or if the logged word is in quotes. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r3: Find the if that tests one letter of the word. The letter may be word[i], or the loop variable of a for...of loop (for (const ch of word) { if (ch === 'r') ...). Is count increased (count++, count += 1 or count = count + 1) inside the body of that if? YES for both forms. NO if the count is increased outside the if. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r1: Ignore any console.log that is only a heading or label (like "My answers:"). Among the remaining logs, is the FIRST one the text SQL (any capital letters)? Code in comments never runs.
questions.r2: Ignore any console.log that is only a heading or label (like "My answers:"). Among the remaining logs, is the SECOND one the text Swift (any capital letters)? Code in comments never runs.
questions.r4: Ignore any console.log that is only a heading or label (like "My answers:"). Among the remaining logs, is the FOURTH one the text JavaScript (any capital letters, or Javascript)? Code in comments never runs.
questions.r5: Ignore any console.log that is only a heading or label (like "My answers:"). Among the remaining logs, is the FIFTH one the text Python (any capital letters)? Code in comments never runs.

questions.r2: Can a king move backwards: does the forward-only rule check skip kings, so that a piece shown as a capital letter (R or B) is allowed to move in both directions, up and down the board? YES if a king is let through the direction check (isKing, a capital-letter test, or a direction that is either way for a king). NO if every piece is held to forward-only, or kings are never made. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.

questions.r4: Does the step direction depend on whose piece it is: red must move up the screen (the row number gets smaller) and black down (the row number gets bigger)? YES if the rule picks a direction from the colour or the turn (like dir = turn === 'r' ? -1 : 1) and the move must match it. NO if one fixed direction is used for both colours, or if any direction is allowed. Code inside a comment, or inside quotes or backticks as text, never runs.
